| [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md) v2 | Bourrat — Reproducees, reproducers, Darwinian individuals | Bourrat builds a nested vocabulary. | [NOTE-131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-131.md) v3 | Schwitzgebel — If materialism is true, the US is conscious | A conditional, informal argument. Any materialist criterion liberal enough to credit rabbits (and rabbit-level distributed aliens, the "squidbits") and behaviourally human-like but oddly built aliens (Sirian supersquids, Antarean antheads) with consciousness also credits the United States. On this argument the US meets the usual materialist marks of consciousness: sophisticated information processing (roughly 10^14 person-to-person visual "connections", comparable to the brain's about 10^14 synapses), goal-directed environmental responsiveness, self-representation and historical embedding. The only exits are eliminativism, extreme sparseness or neurochauvinism, each costlier than the conclusion. The paper argues for no universal criterion. It ends undecided between three readings: US consciousness, a challenge to materialists, or grounds to distrust universal metaphysics of mind. | Read |
| [NOTE-134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-134.md) v3 | Carroll — Reality as a vector in Hilbert space | A programmatic essay, not a result paper. Carroll argues that a quantum theory is fixed, up to unitary equivalence, by the Hamiltonian's eigenvalue list {E_n} on a finite-dimensional factor (he assumes a non-degenerate spectrum), and that parts are not given. Subsystems (tensor factorisations H = H_S ⊗ H_E or ⨂_α H_α), classicality and space are to be selected afterwards as rare structure that suits the dynamics. The only uniqueness he reports is for local factorisations, and it rests on a cited theorem (Cotler et al. 2019). The system/environment criterion rests on "simple numerical examples" in a companion paper, the metric and Einstein's equation on "optimistic assumptions", and emergent fields on a hope. | Read |

| [NOTE-151](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-151.md) v2 | Register — The Depth of the Body | Register argues that body parthood "for moral purposes" is bounded below by depth. | [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md) v2 | SEP — Mereology | The entry argues that no mereological principle, not even the partial-order core M (Reflexivity, Transitivity, Antisymmetry), is merely a fixing of the meaning of "part". | [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md) v2 | Griesemer & Shavit — Scaffolding individuality (3Cs) | The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. Table 1 puts the transition to a new level of individuality between stages 2 and 3 only. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. Its one argued conclusion is hedged: community-level inheritance "seem[s] likely to evolve in tandem" with community-level individuality (§3). | Read |

| [NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md) | 'What is a Thing?': Topos Theory in the Foundations of Physics | The Döring–Isham programme in one volume. | [NOTE-338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-338.md) | Where Am I? | A first-person story with an argument inside. With his brain in a vat in Houston radio-linked to his body under Tulsa, the narrator tests three answers to "where am I?": where the body is, where the brain is, where the point of view is. He favours the third and finds it unclear. A computer duplicate of his brain can take over his body with no detectable difference, and when duplicate and brain drift out of step there are two persons in one body. Intuition pumps, no thesis defended to the end. | Read |
| [NOTE-339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-339.md) | Examining the Society of Mind | An exposition, read in full. Singh dates the Society of Mind to Minsky and Papert's early-1970s robot work, finds its agent in the procedure-bearing frame of 1974, and quotes the unpublished 1976 book drafts. He sorts the 1986 book's mechanisms into agents, simplest agents, agency construction, problem solving, communication and growth. Agents need no shared code: K-lines, randomly wired buses and paranomes stand in for messages. He finds near-relatives in Bayes nets, case-based reasoning, blackboards, Cyc and Soar, and concludes that the theory has never been implemented. Its claims of lineage are asserted, not shown. | Read |

| [NOTE-341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md) | The Computational Boundary of a "Self" | A hypothesis essay. A Self is the set of parts that pursue goals together, and its boundary is the farthest region of space and time it can measure and act on, its "cognitive light cone". | [NOTE-342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-342.md) | Chalmers — Does a rock implement every finite-state automaton? | Implementation needs strong, counterfactual-supporting conditionals for every transition in the table, not one run, so Putnam's rock does not implement every FSA. Repaired, the triviality result survives for weak formalisms. A clock plus a dial implements every inputless FSA. The right input–output dependencies plus an input memory and a dial implement every FSA with those dependencies. Combinatorial-state automata, with independently varying components in distinct physical regions, demand fine-grained causal structure, and a blind implementation must grow exponentially. Logically possible false implementations and an overstrict independence condition are left open. Minds attach to (system, CSA) pairs, so the Chinese room holds two. | Read |
| [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md) | Rupert — Challenges to the Hypothesis of Extended Cognition | Rupert separates extended cognition (HEC) from embedded cognition (HEMC) and from content externalism, then argues that HEC loses to HEMC on conservatism. | [NOTE-347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-347.md) | Chalmers — Absent Qualia, Fading Qualia, Dancing Qualia | Organizational invariance, that fine-grained functional isomorphs of a conscious system have the same experiences, is defended by reductio over gradual neuron replacement. | [NOTE-348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) | The Emotion Machine | Read in the 2005 draft. Emotions are Ways to Think: each emotional state is a selection of mental resources turned on and off, made by Selectors that Critics trigger when they recognise a type of problem, and ordinary thinking uses the same switching. On this design sit six levels of mental activity, panalogies that link descriptions across realms, and a Self that is a network of partial models. It is argued by example and analogy, with no experiment and few neural claims. Against Damasio, the body is a resource the brain exploits, not what an emotion is made of; on Elliot it proposes, without evidence, the reverse causal direction. | Read |
| [NOTE-349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md) | Searle — Minds, brains, and programs | A man who follows English rules for manipulating Chinese symbols can answer Chinese questions like a native speaker without understanding Chinese, so no program is by itself sufficient for understanding. The argument concerns intentionality, and its answer to the systems reply rests on treating the internalised system as a part of the man, which is the point in dispute. | Read |
| [NOTE-351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-351.md) | Intelligence without representation | A methodological manifesto with working robots behind it. Brooks argues that AI should build complete autonomous Creatures incrementally and test them in the real world, and that intelligence should be decomposed into parallel activity-producing layers, each running from sensing to action, not into perception, central reasoning and action. His robots have no central representation or control, and their coherence exists "in the eye of an observer", as in Minsky's account of human behaviour. The evidence is three layers on one robot, described, not measured, and the broad hypothesis about representation is flagged as a hypothesis. | Read |
| [NOTE-352](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-352.md) | K-Lines: A Theory of Memory | Memory as reinstatement: a K-line, attached on a memorable event to the agents then active, later re-imposes that partial mental state. K-lines build on earlier K-lines into a K-pyramid against the perceptual P-pyramid; cross-exclusion makes conflicting details cancel into abstraction; learning needs a third, goal-holding net. A programme statement: no simulation, and the P→K link is left unspecified. | Read |
| [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md) | Chalmers — Extended Cognition and Extended Consciousness | Chalmers restates the 1998 extended-mind thesis as a claim about constitution through sensorimotor interaction, because the original statement is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that the critics accept. | [NOTE-358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-358.md) | Chalmers — The combination problem for panpsychism | A taxonomy, not a solution. The combination problem is three problems (subject, quality, structure) plus four smaller ones (unity, boundary, awareness, grain). Each yields an argument against constitutive panpsychism, and subject-summing and structural mismatch are the strongest. Responses fall into emergent, autonomous, identity and combinatorial panpsychism. The non-combinatorial ones pay in mental causation or revised physics. Phenomenal bonding, quantum holism, small palettes and informational composition are judged most promising, but none is shown to work. James's argument at its origin is an argument against group minds, and a footnote objects to IIT's exclusion postulate that it makes consciousness extrinsic. | Read |
| [NOTE-362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-362.md) v2 | Kammerer — How a materialist can deny that the US is probably conscious | The Sophisticated Anti-Nesting Principle. A whole W with a functional property P that would normally suffice for conscious state S lacks S if some part of W plays a role that (A) requires the part to have conscious states representing W and (B) is needed for W to have P (or any other property sufficient for S). The SAP leaves the antheads and Block's tiny-people brain conscious, permits some group consciousness, and denies the US conscious states because its citizens represent it and could not be replaced by parts that do not. Its defence is an Occam-style rule against ascribing consciousness where other subjects' states explain the behaviour, plus a tu quoque on residual arbitrariness. | Read |
| [NOTE-364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-364.md) | The Self as a Center of Narrative Gravity | A self is an abstractum like a centre of gravity, posited by interpretation, and like a fictional character it is indeterminate beyond what its story fixes. A mindless novel-writing robot can author a self whose story is true of the robot. Brains are bundles of partly autonomous systems that make themselves cohere into one autobiography, and when the story coheres around two points there are two selves. The essay argues by analogy and thought experiment. Its evolutionary account of self-talk is speculation, and its evidence is cited. | Read |
| [NOTE-365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-365.md) | Integrated Information Theory 3.0 | The 2014 restatement of IIT. Five axioms of experience become five postulates about mechanisms in a state, and an experience is identified with the maximally irreducible conceptual structure of a complex. Exclusion is the anti-nesting rule: of all overlapping sets of elements, only the one with locally maximal Φ is conscious, so no subset or superset of a complex is. It is postulated from the axiom that experience has definite borders; Occam's razor is invoked only for exclusion within a mechanism. Logic-gate examples give minor complexes, a conscious inactive network, a minimally conscious photodiode and a feed-forward zombie. Nothing larger than about a dozen elements is computable. | Read |
| [NOTE-366](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-366.md) | Block — Troubles with Functionalism | Functionalism fixes mental states only by their relations to inputs and outputs, so a body run by a billion radio-linked people, each executing one line of your machine table, is functionally equivalent to you. There is prima facie doubt that it has qualia, and Block argues the doubt has a rational basis: it is unlike us in psychology and neurophysiology, and it was built to mimic us. The doubt does not depend on the parts having minds. Putnam's anti-nesting stipulation is an ad hoc patch that fails in every version Block tries. Psychofunctionalism secures beliefs but perhaps not qualia, and no account of inputs and outputs avoids both liberalism and chauvinism. | Read |
| [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md) | Adams & Aizawa — The bounds of cognition | Adams and Aizawa grant [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md)'s parity sentence but deny that any actual case meets it. Otto's inscriptions have only derived content, Otto's retrieval uses vision and motor control that Inga's does not, and coupling a process to its surroundings does not extend it. So cognition is brain-bound as a contingent fact, and human-plus-tool systems are too motley for a science. | Read |
| [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md) | Chalmers — Foreword to Supersizing the Mind | Ten years after [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), its co-author says the iPhone has made the thesis vivid, that the only principled objection is the perception-action boundary, and that the right reply is to let belief-ascription follow explanatory purpose, so that Otto's belief is extended for some explanations and not others. | [NOTE-373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-373.md) | Survival and Identity | What matters in survival is the R-relation (mental continuity and connectedness among person-stages), and it is also identity, because persons are maximal R-interrelated aggregates of stages and so the relation of being stages of one person is the R-relation. | [NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md) | Personal Identity | A survey of the persistence debate with an animalist's emphasis. Fission and the too-many-thinkers objection are the two arguments that do the work. It avoids the word "self". One in-text citation (Olson and Witt 2020) has no matching bibliography entry. | Read |
| [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) | Adams & Aizawa — Defending the Bounds of Cognition | A reply to a manuscript of Clark's "Memento's Revenge". | [NOTE-381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-381.md) | Schwitzgebel — Is the United States Phenomenally Conscious? Reply to Kammerer | Three concerns about Kammerer's Sophisticated Anti-Nesting Principle. It may not exclude actual groups, even the US, because citizens may not consciously represent the concrete entity at issue. Condition A's "required" makes group consciousness depend on members' motives: read loosely it gives flickering consciousness with no group-level change, read strictly it can never be met. The Occam-style justification either generalises into causal exclusion or is ad hoc, and group-level explanation is often simpler. Kammerer's is still the best anti-nesting principle the author has met. | Read |
| [NOTE-385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-385.md) | Of Identity and Diversity | Identity is relative to the idea the name stands for: same mass, same life (oak, horse, man), same consciousness (person). A person is a thinking being that "can consider itself as itself", and personal identity reaches as far back as consciousness can be extended, independent of substance. Man and person come apart (prince and cobbler; day-man and night-man), and "person" is "a forensic term" grounding reward and punishment. Argued from cases and intuitions; "the same consciousness" is never defined. | Read |
| [NOTE-386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-386.md) | Of Personal Identity | No impression of a self is constant, so there is no idea of one; introspection finds only perceptions, and the mind is "a bundle or collection of different perceptions". Its ascribed identity is a fiction of the imagination, like that of ships, churches and plants, produced by resemblance and causation, with memory discovering rather than producing it; hard cases are "grammatical". The Appendix confesses that two principles, the distinctness of perceptions and the imperceptibility of real connexions, leave the unity of the mind unexplained. | Read |
| [NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md) | Ritchie — Social Structures and the Ontology of Social Groups | A structuralist framework for social groups. A social structure is a network of relations constitutively dependent on social factors; it can be overt or covert, intentionally or unintentionally created and instantiated, internal or external to what realizes it. Organized social groups are structured wholes whose internal social structures people occupy; feature social groups are social kinds, nodes in external social structures, which can be intersectional. A restriction to structures that intuitively exist or figure in explanations keeps arbitrary collections out. Motivated, not proved; nothing on agency or minds. | Read |
| [NOTE-390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-390.md) | Ritchie — What are groups? | Six criteria for any theory of groups (members vary across times and worlds; groups are temporary, contingent and located; coincident groups of one kind can be distinct) rule out groups as non-singular pluralities, fusions, Burge aggregates and Effingham's sets. Proposed: a group is a realization of a structure whose nodes are defined by functional relations; it exists while every node is occupied, members are the occupiers, and two groups are identical at a time only with the same members in the same relations. A sketch of a view, silent on agency. | Read |
| [NOTE-393](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-393.md) | Epstein — Social Ontology (SEP) | A survey organised by its author's own distinction: what grounds a social fact versus what anchors the category it falls under. It reports that ontological individualism is widely assumed and now contested; that grounding has displaced supervenience; that convention, collective acceptance, patterns, practices and language are rival theories of anchoring; and that whether anchoring is a distinct relation is disputed. It covers groups, group agency, institutions, race and gender, artifacts, money, law and language. Survey claims are reported, not argued; one citation (Epstein 2016) is missing from the bibliography, and Schwitzgebel 2015 is listed with critics of group phenomenal states. | Read |
| [NOTE-468](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-468.md) | Biological organisation as closure of constraints | A constraint acts on a process while being conserved at that process's time scale; closure is a set of constraints, each directly dependent on and generative for another, that cannot be split. This separates closure from cycles of processes, grounds functions, and gives a boundary criterion, refined by a preliminary count-based tendency to closure for symbionts and by nested separated closures for levels. Applied only to schematic examples; closure is not claimed to define organisms. | Read |
| [NOTE-550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-550.md) | List & Pettit — Group Agency and Supervenience | Four conditions of agency (§2). A group's judgments supervene on members' contributions under a constitution (§3). With a universal domain, robust group rationality is inconsistent with majoritarian, uniform proposition-wise and proposition-wise supervenience (Propositions 1–3), and consistent with set-wise supervenience, as the premise-based and distributed premise-based procedures show (Propositions 4–5; Table 4). The group's judgment on a conclusion can be fixed by members' judgments on premises alone. Emergent agency without members' conception of the group is judged unintelligible (§6). | Read |
| [NOTE-555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-555.md) | Conceptualization of the Holobiont Paradigm as It Pertains to Corals | A mini-review arguing that corals must be studied as holobionts. The holobiont is defined by location (coral plus microbiota in body, mucus and skeleton), and its membership can change. Traits belong to host–symbiont combinations: a novel anemone–alga pairing out-performed both natural ones in oxygen flux at 32–34 °C, and two octocorals lost symbionts by different routes, one per host cell and one with host cells. It asks, without answering, whether the holobiont is the unit of selection. | Read |
